summary:
The Secure America Act, Pub. L. 119-98, provides reconciliation appropriations for fiscal year 2026 to the Department of Homeland Security, primarily for U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) and U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE), with all amounts stated as in addition to amounts otherwise available, appropriated from unobligated Treasury funds, and generally available through September 30, 2029. The Act does not amend the United States Code, but funds activities under specified existing statutory authorities.

Title I appropriates funds for activities other than immigration enforcement and customs functions. Section 101 appropriates $9.55 billion to the CBP Commissioner to hire, pay, train, and equip Border Patrol agents and support personnel for non-immigration-enforcement and non-customs functions, and prohibits use of those funds after October 31, 2028, to recruit, hire, or train personnel for processing coordinator duties. Section 102 appropriates $7.45 billion to the ICE Director for Homeland Security Investigations agents, support personnel, mission support, and operations and maintenance, excluding immigration-enforcement and customs-enforcement missions; within that amount, $108.5 million is directed to child exploitation investigators and forensic analysts, victim identification and rescue activities, and related training at specified HSI components. Section 103 appropriates $3.45 billion to CBP for specified border security technology and screening purposes, including nonintrusive inspection equipment, AI and machine-learning technologies, Air and Marine Operations platforms, border surveillance technology, the biometric entry-exit system under section 7208 of the Intelligence Reform and Terrorism Prevention Act of 2004 (8 U.S.C. 1365b), drug-trafficking interdiction, and CBP non-immigration/non-customs mission support. It bars procurement or deployment of southwest or northern border surveillance towers not tested and accepted by CBP to deliver “autonomous” capabilities, which the section defines. Section 104 appropriates $2.5 billion to the Secretary of Homeland Security for Title I purposes.

Title II appropriates funds for immigration enforcement. Section 201 appropriates $13.02 billion to CBP for personnel and necessary mission support, operations, and maintenance to carry out immigration enforcement activities. Section 202 appropriates $31.075 billion to ICE for immigration enforcement personnel across directorates; transportation for alien departure or removal; IT, facility, and fleet maintenance and sustainment; expansion and implementation of Immigration and Nationality Act section 287(g), 8 U.S.C. 1357(g), agreements; Office of the Principal Legal Advisor attorneys and support staff; and immigration-enforcement mission support. Section 202(9) reserves not less than $350 million for ICE expenses relating to covered unlawful aliens in jurisdictions that are not “qualified cooperating jurisdictions,” excludes Indian tribal governments from that classification, defines that term by reference to section 287(g) agreements or certifications of compliance with 8 U.S.C. 1373 and 8 U.S.C. 1644, restricts use of those funds to facilitate release except as required by existing law, and defines “covered unlawful alien” by reference to specified INA inadmissibility, deportability, detention, detainer, and illegal-entry/reentry provisions. Section 203 appropriates $2.5 billion to DHS for Title II purposes or for paragraph (3) or (7) of section 100051 of Pub. L. 119-21.
